title: partial-site-failover-smoke-tests-tf-compatibility-validation-harness
content:
Purpose / scope:
This is a working draft for a lightweight, repeatable validation harness used during partial site failovers for Private Deployments (VPC/on-prem). The goal is to give SREs and on-call engineers a simple set of terraform-compatible steps + smoke-tests to confirm critical liveness and data-continuity properties after an infrastructure-level failover or when reprovisioning a subset of services (e.g., control-plane in region A, workers in region B).

Why this is different from full snapshot/restore runbooks:
- Focused on partial-site failover scenarios (not full cluster rehydrate).
- Emphasizes quick confidence checks that cover control-plane, model-serving runtime hot-path, and state-forwarding (WAL/KV replay sanity).
- Includes a compatibility checklist for current terraform modules so infra changes don’t break DR playbooks.

Assumptions:
- Terraform modules used are from repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/private-deploy-modules.git
- Remote state is stored in GCS/S3 with state locking enabled (locks via backend config).
- Artifact store (models + container images) is reachable from failover site or pre-cached per air-gapped instructions.
- Prometheus + Loki (or an equivalent metrics/log collector) are available for verification metrics.
- Secrets are available via customer KMS/HSM or pre-seeded vault in DR environment.

Prereqs (quick checklist):
- terraform workspace selected: terraform workspace select dr-<customer>-<date>
- confirm remote state backend reachable and unlocked: terraform init && terraform plan
- ensure runbook owner (on-call) has SSH and KMS access
- artifacts: models checksum file available (sha256 sums), container digests recorded

TF module compatibility notes (quick matrix):
- modules/network-vpc: v1.3.x is DR-safe (route table refs stable). Breaking change in v1.4: renaming of nat_gateway_id output — if customer uses module output for external routing, pre-apply a compatibility wrapper or pin to v1.3.x.
- modules/storage-state: requires backend migration helper when switching between GCS <-> S3. Use helper script: infra/tools/state-migrate.sh --validate before doing any lock changes.
- modules/serving-runtime: v2.0+ includes new kv-cache provider and different IAM bindings — ensure terraform var enable_kv_cache = true only when runtime is upgraded in tandem.
- modules/kafka-cluster: must preserve broker IDs in TF state; when reprovisioning, pass preserve_broker_ids = true to avoid partition reassignment churn.

Validation harness (high level):
1) Minimal infra bringup (target subset):
   - terraform apply -target=module.network -target=module.storage -target=module.control-plane -var-file=dr-vars.tfvars
   - Notes: Keep apply durations small — we only want enough infra for health endpoints and message bus connectivity.

2) Quick schema/metadata checks (0-10m):
   - auth: curl -sSf https://control-plane.internal/health | jq .version
   - model artifacts: aws s3 ls s3://artifacts/<customer>/<model>/ --recursive and verify sha256sums against /opt/dr-manifests/checksums.txt
   - DB connectivity: run sql-sanity.sh --db ${DB_CONN} (script does a create temp table, insert, select, drop)

3) KV cache warm + KV-forwarded requests (10-25m):
   - rehydrate prefix cache (if available): tools/cache-populate --source s3://<cache-bucket> --target http://cache.internal/prefill
   - send a batch of representative requests: ./tools/dr-harness/send-requests.sh --profile quick-smoke --concurrency 4 --duration 60s
   - Expected: 95th percentile latency < target_slo, error rate < 0.5%

4) Streaming/generation smoke (25-40m):
   - run stream-health-checker: ./tools/stream-check --endpoint https://runtime.internal/stream --timeout 30s
   - verify that function/tool-calling hooks return expected structured JSON for 90% of samples

5) Data-forwarding sanity (WAL replay / Kafka lag):
   - check consumer groups: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe | grep consumer-group-main
   - ensure lag < 1000 messages or within previously observed baseline; if lag spikes, run kafka-reassign-plan.sh to rebalance (manual step, see below)

6) End-to-end smoke (40-60m):
   - end-to-end sample: curl -X POST https://api.internal/v1/generate -d '@testvectors/e2e-small.json'
   - verify token accounting: compare /metrics endpoint counter increments and per-route cost counters in console.

Failure modes and immediate mitigations:
- Terraform state lock missing / remote backend not reachable: abort; use infra/tools/inspect-backend.sh to gather diagnostics and open JIRA-DR for state-ops.
- Model artifact checksum mismatch: try to re-pull from artifact store; if air-gapped, use USB-transfer and run tools/artifact-verify --install <tarball>.
- Kafka consumer lag high: check broker connectivity, then run kafka-tools/consumer-lag-repair.sh in read-only mode to get suggested reassignment. Only run actual reassignment if maintenance window.
- Secrets fetch failing: rotate to fallback service account creds captured in dr-vars.tfvars.fallback and escalate to security.

Upgrade sequencing guidance during a partial failover:
- Never upgrade runtime code and terraform modules in the same window. Sequence: 1) pin terraform modules to compatibility tag; 2) bring infra up; 3) deploy runtime containers; 4) run smoke harness; 5) if stable, upgrade modules one at a time with canary flag.
- Example: to upgrade serving-runtime in DR environment:
  a) set var runtime_image = "gcr.io/redwood/serving-runtime:v2026-02-15-canary" in dr-vars and run deploy to canary hosts only
  b) run smoke harness against canary instances (subset of traffic)
  c) roll out to remaining nodes if checks pass

Rollback primitives (fast):
- Infra rollback: terraform apply using pinned state version: terraform workspace select dr-<...> && terraform state pull > state.json && terraform state push --force state.json (only after confirmation from state team).
- Runtime rollback: deploy previous container digest from digests.txt via kubectl set image or job-based rolling deploy script: tools/k8s/rollout-rollback.sh --deployment runtime --image <digest>

Air-gapped specifics (short):
- Provide pre-bundled tarball: artifacts.tar.gz (models/, images-manifests/, checksums.txt). Use tools/offline/install-artifacts.sh to place artifacts into local registry and update manifests.
- TLS and KMS: if KMS is unavailable, use sealed-secrets fallback and ensure private keys are stored in /var/lib/dr-keys with strict permissions.

Runbook checklist (what to log during an event):
- event_id, owner, time-of-first-detection, suspected-cause
- terraform commands run + stdout/stderr dumps (store under /var/log/dr-ops/<event_id>)
- smoke-test run ids and pass/fail summary (attach metrics snapshots GIFs or CSV)
- model checksums and container digests used
- any manual db migrations run and migration hashes

Quick diagnostics commands (cheat sheet):
- terraform plan (dr): terraform plan -var-file=dr-vars.tfvars -out=plan.tfout
- SSH jump: ssh -J alice@bastion.internal ops@node-03.internal
- check pod health: kubectl get pods -n redwood | egrep "runtime|control-plane"
- query metrics: curl -s http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=up

Automation ideas / TODOs (future improvements):
- Add an automated terraform smoke-apply pipeline with a dry-run gate that posts to Slack and requires ack before irreversible ops. (ticket: JIRA-DR-1377)
- Extend dr-harness to produce structured JSON results and upload to S3 for postmortem analysis.
- Implement an artifact prefetcher that can be scheduled during low-cost windows so air-gapped caches are kept warm.

Post-event postmortem template (short):
- timeline, root cause, detection path, what went well, what failed, follow-ups (owners + due dates).

Notes / rough bookmarks for runbook authors:
- Keep smoke-tests as small as possible; aim for a 60-minute max time-to-confidence.
- For customers with strict RTO < 30m, pre-stage warmed nodes and use blue-green control-plane switch-over rather than rebuilds.
- Keep a current list of module compatibility patches in repo: infra/docs/dr-module-compat.md (maintainer: @MarcoRivera).

Appendix: helpful scripts referenced above (location summaries)
- infra/tools/state-migrate.sh
- tools/dr-harness/send-requests.sh
- tools/stream-check
- kafka-tools/consumer-lag-repair.sh
- tools/offline/install-artifacts.sh
- tools/k8s/rollout-rollback.sh

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we want an opt-in flag in modules/serving-runtime to automatically enable KV cache prefill during terraform apply? (pros: faster warm; cons: complexity in infra lifecycle)
- Should we keep a dedicated DR S3/GCS bucket per-customer or use a regional aggregated bucket with RBAC?

Contact / escalation paths:
- primary oncall: #eng-sre (paginated)
- DR leads: Sofia Patel (owner), Marco Rivera (terraform lead)
- security escalation: priya.nair@redwood.com

End of doc - draft.
